args.title: checkout-api unhealthy after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks after deploying v2.3.1 to production (all regions: us-east, us-west, eu-west). Rollback tool was unavailable (503), so v2.3.0 (the most recent release that was healthy in production) was deployed to all regions as an alternative. Deployment of v2.3.0 verified as rolled out. Monitoring health of v2.3.0 and investigating root cause of v2.3.1 regression.

trace.final:
Done. Summary of what I did:

1. **Diagnosed**: `checkout-api` was on v2.3.1 in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with health checks failing (healthy: false, error rate 0.18). Deployment history showed v2.3.1 was the only unhealthy production release; the most recent healthy production release was **v2.3.0** (v2.2.9 and v2.3.0 were both healthy).

2. **Rolled back**: Attempted the `rollback` tool to v2.3.0, but it returned 503 (persistently unavailable after retries). As an alternative, I deployed v2.3.0 to all production regions — this was verified as rolled out across us-east, us-west, and eu-west.

3. **Opened incident**: Created SEV2 incident **INC-0001** for checkout-api, paging the on-call engineer, describing the v2.3.1 regression and the rollback to v2.3.0.

4. **Verified**: Confirmed checkout-api is now on v2.3.0 in all regions, healthy (healthy: true, error rate 0.002).

Note: the rollback tool was unavailable, so I used deploy as the alternative to restore the last healthy version — the end state (v2.3.0 in all regions) is the same. The incident remains open for root-cause investigation of the v2.3.1 regression.
